Requirements got initially in via #1154 / #1156 https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/commit/367d6feb812d072c2837293066230c8b8f894b4b

I reopen, as I think those requirements needs some explanation into those that is clearly understandable, which vector those mitigate or why they exists.

Currently those are located in "V13.7 HTTP/2"

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **13.7.1** | [ADDED] Verify that the value in the Content-Length request header field matches the calculated length using the built-in mechanism. | 1 | 400 |
| **13.7.2** | [ADDED] Verify that all Transfer-Encoding header fields are stripped from the message or that the request is blocked entirely. | 1 | |
| **13.7.3** | [ADDED] Verify that a full CRLF (\r\n) sequence is neutralized inside a HTTP/2 header. | 1 | 113 |

More things:
* 13.7.1 - what means "built-in mechanism"
* 13.7.2 - the point is that application or web server must not use the header field value - options are - remove the header field, ignore it, block entire request?

If these requirements are applicable to HTTP/2, I think this should be stated in the requirement if we want the requirements to be self-contained (i.e. that they can be interpreted correctly without looking at the title of the section they are located in).

For example:

> [ADDED] Verify that the value in the Content-Length request header field *of HTTP/2 requests* matches the actual length of the request using the frameworks built-in validation mechanism. This is to prevent HTTP request smuggling attacks.

> * Neither CR nor LF are allowed in [field names](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-field-names);

This applies to CR, LF and CRLF for both field names and values. Perhaps a change?

I tried to come up with something but I'm not so happy with it:

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **4.2.1** |Verify that all application components—including load balancers, firewalls, and application servers—determine boundaries of incoming HTTP messages using the appropriate mechanism for the HTTP version to prevent HTTP request smuggling. In HTTP/1.x, if a Transfer-Encoding header field is present, the Content-Length header MUST be ignored per RFC 2616. When using HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, if a  Content-Length header field is present, the receiver must ensure that it is consistent with the length of the DATA frames. | 2 | v5.0.be-13.6.2 |
| **4.3.1** | Verify that the the sender of a HTTP message does not produce HTTP messages with a Content-Length header field conflicting with the length of the content as determined by the framing of the HTTP protocol, in order to prevent request smuggling attacks. This applies to chunked encoding in HTTP/1 ad the message framing of HTTP/2 and HTTP/3. | 3 | v5.0.be-13.7.1 |
| **4.3.2** | Verify that a HTTP endpoint does not generate HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 messages with connection-specific header fields such as Transfer-Encoding to prevent response splitting and header injection attacks. | 3 | v5.0.be-13.7.2 |
| **4.3.3** | Verify that HTTP/2 header field names and values do not contain any CR (\r), LF (\n), or CRLF (\r\n) sequences. If any such characters are detected, the header must be rejected or sanitized to prevent header injection attacks. | 3 | v5.0.be-13.7.3 |

Some notes:

* In this form, 4.3.1 should be moved into 4.2.
* For 4.3.2, I kept "response splitting and header injection attacks". Is "header injection attacks" relevant in here?
* I used "endpoint" here consistent with RFC 9112 and RFC 9113. This is supposed to talk about a HTTP client-or-server-or-proxy. However, HTTP endpoint is often understood to mean "a URL + method" instead os we may want to change that.
